title: Bram and the Bridge
premise: In 1893, Tamsin Ishikawa, a half-Japanese apprentice clockmaker in the river town of Marlow's Bend, is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock just as autumn floods close the bridge—the town's only road out. Trapped inside the observatory with the quarreling Harrow family, whose patriarch is dying and whose will names an heir no one expected, Tamsin discovers the clock's mechanism has been deliberately sabotaged to falsify the time of death that decides the inheritance. As the floodwaters rise and the family closes ranks, Tamsin must choose between exposing the truth—which would ruin the one person who ever showed them kindness—and repairing the clock, which would seal an innocent heir out of her birthright. In the end, Tamsin rebuilds the escapement to tell the truth, testifies before the town magistrate at great personal cost, and leaves Marlow's Bend on the reopened bridge as the clock strikes noon, carrying neither inheritance nor apology but their own name, spoken aloud for the first time.
about_author: L. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former horologist's assistant who spent a decade restoring tower clocks across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. Their work explores quiet acts of justice in communities bound by rivers, clocks, and secrets.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A letter arrives from the Harrow Observatory requesting their master for a repair; when he falls ill, Tamsin goes alone, concealing their half-blood under a borrowed coat and their master's name. The beat is anxious hope: first chance to prove skill the guild denies them.

chapters.title: Twelve Bells, Thirteen Ticks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climbing the observatory tower, they find the master clock striking wrong—one tick too many—and sense deliberate tampering in the escapement. Old Mr. Harrow watches from his chair, saying nothing. Beat: unease sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The House That Faces Away
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Settling into the observatory household, Tamsin maps its silences: the eldest son Edmund's cold courtesy, daughter Verity's watchfulness, the housekeeper Mrs. Pell's kindness. Beat: learning the rules of a new silence.

chapters.title: Water at the Tollgate
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Autumn rains swell the river; the bridge closes for the season, stranding everyone. Verity resents the stranger tinkering above while her father declines. Beat: claustrophobia and suspicion.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Request
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Mr. Harrow privately asks Tamsin to make the clock keep true time 'for what comes after,' pressing a brass key into their hand. Beat: the weight of being trusted by someone powerful.

chapters.title: Edmund's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund reviews the estate accounts and the draft will naming Verity heir—a choice he believes madness. He visits the clock room at night. Beat: cold ambition dressed as duty.

chapters.title: What the Escapement Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Disassembling the movement, Tamsin finds filed teeth and a shifted pallet—sabotage designed to make the clock run slow, distorting any recorded hour. Beat: dread; someone inside wants time itself to lie.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell's POV. Over bread and stew, Mrs. Pell tells Tamsin about the Harrows' dead mother and hints that the will was rewritten twice. She treats Tamsin without flinching at their face or name. Beat: warmth, fragile and dangerous.

chapters.title: The First Flood Warning
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Rivermen shout warnings from the far bank; the bridge is impassable for weeks. Cut off, Tamsin realizes whatever happens in this house cannot be escaped or reported until spring. Beat: isolation closing like a fist.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Clock Room
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Catching Edmund tampering again, Tamsin hides and watches him adjust the pendulum—then sees Verity watching too, from the stair. Three people now share a secret none will name. Beat: complicity.

chapters.title: Verity's Bargain
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Verity confronts Tamsin: she knows they are not who the letter said. She offers silence in exchange for help proving Edmund altered the will's witness page. Beat: alliance built on mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Hour of Death
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Mr. Harrow dies at dawn; the falsified clock will place his death an hour earlier—invalidating the witnessed signing of the final will. Tamsin holds the truth in their hands and says nothing. Beat: guilt's first taste.

chapters.title: Reading of the Paper
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With the timing disputed, the older will stands; Edmund claims the estate. His triumph tastes like ash—he did not expect to feel watched by the clock itself. Beat: victory curdling.

chapters.title: The Key in the Escapement
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Alone with the movement, Tamsin discovers Mr. Harrow's brass key fits a hidden register: the clock has been recording every tampering in punched brass discs. The dying man planned ahead. Beat: awe and terror—evidence exists, but using it destroys Mrs. Pell's son, the coerced accomplice.

chapters.title: A Debt in the Village Below
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell's POV. Flashback chapter: how her son Tobias, deep in gambling debt, was pressured into filing the escapement. Beat: a mother's terrible arithmetic—her boy's freedom against an innocent woman's inheritance.

chapters.title: Rising Water, Rising Stakes
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. The flood breaches the lower road; the household evacuates to the tower. Edmund burns papers in the grate. Verity begs Tamsin to act before the evidence drowns with everything else. Beat: urgency compressing all choices.

chapters.title: Which Silence Keeps You Safe
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin weighs twelve years of learned silences against the punched brass discs in their pocket. A near-drowning on the flooded stair forces the decision: some silences kill. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Clock Tells the Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climax begins: before the assembled family, Tamsin repairs the escapement publicly, restores true time, and plays the register discs—each tampering dated and initialed by the machine itself. Beat: the apprentice's hands finally steadier than the master's.

chapters.title: Magistrate in a Wet Coat
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The magistrate arrives by boat; testimony is taken by lamplight in the tower. Edmund implicates Tobias; Tamsin insists coercion be weighed. Beat: justice arriving imperfect, outside any clean law.

chapters.title: What Is Owed
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. The final will is upheld; Verity inherits but refuses to press charges against Tobias, paying his debt instead. She offers Tamsin a place and a partnership. Beat: mercy as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Name I Keep
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin declines the offer—not out of fear, but because staying would mean another borrowed name. They sign the repair ledger 'Tamsin Ishikawa' in full view of the household. Beat: identity claimed, quietly.

chapters.title: Noon on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Spring opens the bridge; Tamsin crosses as the repaired master clock strikes noon over the water, carrying tools, the brass key, and nothing owed. Behind them, the tower keeps honest time. Beat: release, and a road finally open.
